generators.carrier: Z-valued 2x2 matrices (chord coordinates of T relative to T_0 on the diamond graph)

relations.statement: det C_T is +1 or -1 for each of the 8 spanning trees T of the diamond graph, i.e. C_T lies in GL(2,Z)
relations.hypotheses: Diamond graph with fixed tree T_0 and b_1 = 2; the check is a finite computation over the 8 trees

relations.statement: det(C_T diag(alpha) C_T^T) = U_G(alpha) for every tree T
relations.hypotheses: Kirchhoff matrix-tree theorem (assumed, cited); alpha positive; the edge labelling puts the shared diagonal edge at alpha = 11

lemmas.statement: The diamond graph has exactly 8 spanning trees. They are the 3-edge subsets other than the two triangles, so the chord pairs are all 10 pairs except the two non-shared edge pairs of the triangles.
With the shared edge weighted 11 and the triangle pairs (2,3) and (5,7), U_G(2,3,5,7,11) = e2(alpha) - 2*3 - 5*7 = 247, and U_G(1,...,1) = 8

near_misses.claim: U = 205 if the shared diagonal edge carries a weight other than 11, e.g. triangles (2,3) and (7,11)
near_misses.rejecting_invariant: The value 247 requires the excluded chord-pair sum to equal 41, which only the shared-edge-11 labelling gives

open_obligations: No existing declarations are available to cite, so all refs are proposed_new
Explicit matrices C_T for the 8 trees and their determinants are not enumerated here
The edge labelling is not given in the target and was inferred from the value 247
Kirchhoff matrix-tree theorem is assumed, not proved
Lean skeletons are arithmetic only and do not formalise the graph
